The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-10 uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which both evaluate to the same literal '[object Object]', so the schema has no index signature or passthrough and Zod strips every field except access_token

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 injects the literal placeholder refresh_token = "refresh_token" overwriting real refresh tokens in sync mode because the stripped schema makes refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token always falsy

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: The CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT response contract is undefined and internally contradictory: the code comment says 'only access token and expiry date' but consumers require per-provider shapes (Google expiry_date, O365 expires_in, Zoom body, Lark envelope, Hubspot token), leaving no implementable spec

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook (lines 28,58) has no HTTP method guard (GET causes unhandled ZodError and 500 instead of 405/400) and no validation of the decrypted payload shape before writing it into credential.key, allowing malformed payloads to silently brick credentials

adjudication.rationale: In newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler has no `req.method` guard and unconditionally runs `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For non-POST requests (e.g., GET where `req.body` is typically empty/undefined), `zod.parse` will throw a `ZodError` that is not caught, resulting in a 500 instead of a controlled 405/400. Additionally, after decrypting `reqBody.keys`, the code does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then writes `key: keys` to `prisma.credential.update/create` without validating the decrypted payload shape, so malformed/incorrect decrypted JSON can be persisted and break/brick downstream credential usage. adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound token request in refreshOAuthTokens.ts (sync mode) carries no authentication while the inbound webhook demands CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, allowing anyone who can reach the endpoint to harvest access tokens for arbitrary user ids

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), Cal.com POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication headers/signature. adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:12-14 has no timeout and no fallback to the native refreshFunction when the sync endpoint is down, so a transient endpoint outage fails all token refreshes across all 9 providers

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the sync-path unconditionally does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when enabled (lines ~6-17) with no `try/catch`, no `AbortController` timeout, and no fallback to `refreshFunction()` on network failure. This is a diff-grounded resilience/availability concern, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect since the intended design may be to hard-depend on the configured sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService.ts:249-258 deletes the diagnostic logging of Microsoft's error response (e.g. AADSTS700009), replacing it with a generic throw that discards the provider's actual error reason, losing debugging signal

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:96 (Google) — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of parsed data, so the Zod wrapper object is persisted as credential.key, breaking refreshAccessToken and permanently breaking Google Calendar integration on first token refresh

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:75-97 (Salesforce) — new unconditional fetch refresh runs on every Salesforce CalendarService instantiation regardless of APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, replacing jsforce's lazy on-401 refresh with an eager network call, an off-flag behavior change to all Salesforce self-hosters

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts (Salesforce) — new code never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so Salesforce credentials are silently excluded from the credential-sync feature the PR claims to deliver, with the exclusion undocumented

adjudication.rationale: In the Salesforce `CalendarService.ts` changes, the refresh flow is implemented with a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`; unlike other integrations in this diff (Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc.), it does not wrap the refresh call with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will not use the credential-sync endpoint. This is a real, diff-grounded incompleteness/scope gap (and is not documented in the diff), but it doesn’t by itself constitute a functional defect in Salesforce’s normal token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-9 — the 'expiry' schema key is the literal string '[object Object]' from calling toString() on a ZodString, so the schema validates only access_token and never an expiry, letting responses missing expiry pass validation and write expiry_date: undefined into stored credentials

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-13 — sync path returns a raw fetch Response while call sites expect provider objects; hubspot reads .refresh_token/.expires_in as undefined causing NaN expiry and setAccessToken(undefined), and lark passes the parent app's response body to handleLarkError as a Lark error envelope — the contract change was not propagated to any caller

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the “sync” branch always does a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw Fetch `Response`, while the non-sync branch returns whatever the passed `refreshFunction()` returns (often a parsed/provider-specific object). This inconsistent return contract is visible in call sites: e.g. `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns the result to `HubspotToken` (a token object) but would receive a `Response` in sync mode; similarly `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` expects `res?.data` (gaxios-like) but would get a Fetch `Response` without `.data`. Also, in `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the sync response (from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) is fed into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which likely expects Lark’s refresh-token HTTP response format, not an arbitrary parent-app endpoint. adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — redirect URI hardcodes '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback' replacing the dynamic appConfig.slug, breaking the ability to repoint the slug via config; unrelated drive-by change traceable to no requirement

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts:25-40 — webhook handler validates only the shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and accepts any userId + any appSlug in appStoreMetadata, so any party with the shared secret can overwrite any user's credentials for any installed app, including apps not in the sync flow; no per-app allowlist or per-user scoping

After that, the caller controls `userId` and `appSlug` (`z.object({ userId, appSlug, keys })`) and the code will `credential.update`/`credential.create` for that `userId` and `appMetadata.slug` with decrypted `keys`, with no per-user scoping/verification beyond “user exists” and no per-app allowlist beyond “app exists + metadata exists”. adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — team-owned OAuth credentials (userId null) are silently excluded from sync: they refresh via the provider path and rotated tokens are never pushed to the parent app, and the receiving webhook only accepts a userId, leaving team-level installs with stale tokens and no error/log/doc

adjudication_records.issue_text: constants.ts:102-103 + refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 + parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:9 — three hand-maintained divergent enablement checks for one feature; setting CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY without CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT yields a state where the webhook accepts writes and validation loosens but refresh still hits the provider; should be a single isCredentialSyncEnabled() source of truth

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse wrapper object ({ success, data }) instead of the parsed data, so the Google caller persists the wrapper as credential.key, corrupting every Google credential on first refresh

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'minimum' schema is syntactically broken: z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]' as a computed key, so the schema validates nothing and zod's strip mode removes all real fields like refresh_token and expiry_date from parsed credentials
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: the Zod object schema is built with computed property keys derived from `z.string().toString()` (and optional variant), which produces a bogus key like "[object Object]" instead of a real field name. This makes the schema invalid/broken and leads to incorrect parsing (and can cause runtime failures).

adjudication_records.issue_text: A literal fake refresh_token: "refresh_token" sentinel is injected when the response lacks a refresh_token and persisted, causing invalid_grant on next refresh and unrecoverable credential death; the previously stored refresh token should be preserved instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which forcibly injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed token response lacks a refresh token (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). Call sites then merge/persist the parsed data. For example, Office365 does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` after `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which will overwrite the previously valid stored refresh token with the literal sentinel. That would cause subsequent refreshes to use an invalid refresh token (likely leading to `invalid_grant`) and makes the credential unrecoverable without re-auth. The finding is directly grounded in the new helper behavior plus the merge logic introduced/used in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync branch in refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response while callers assume incompatible response shapes (gaxios res.data for Google, token object for Hubspot, axios .data for Zoho), causing TypeError, undefined fields, or invalid tokens being persisted

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;` returning a raw `fetch` `Response`. Multiple callers in the diff assume non-`Response` shapes:
- Google Calendar (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) treats the return as a gaxios response: `const token = res?.data;` which will be `undefined` for a `fetch` `Response` (no `.data`), leading to missing `access_token/expiry_date` and bad persistence.
- Hubspot (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`) types the return as `HubspotToken` and uses it as a token object; a `Response` is incompatible.
- Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`) expect an axios response with `.data`; a `fetch` `Response` won’t have `.data`.
So the finding is directly supported by the diff and would cause runtime errors/invalid tokens when the sync branch is exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, syncing credentials against the wrong user

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call to `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and, when syncing is enabled, sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Other integrations consistently pass `credential.userId`. Passing a credential identifier instead of the Cal.com user id would sync/refresh tokens for the wrong user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService now performs an unconditional network token refresh on every service instantiation, adding a remote OAuth round-trip on the hot path and failing construction on transient refresh errors even when the stored access token is valid

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now does a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` unconditionally before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (no expiry/validity check on the existing `credential.key.access_token`). It also throws on any non-"OK" response (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`), meaning service setup can fail due to transient refresh/network errors even if the previously stored access token might still be usable. This introduces a new remote round-trip and a new hard-failure path on initialization/hot path relative to using the stored token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler has a check-then-insert TOCTOU race with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), allowing concurrent deliveries to create duplicate credential rows and cause token flapping and stale credentials

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), credential persistence is implemented as `findFirst` on `{ userId, appId }` followed by either `update` or `create`. This is a classic check-then-act pattern and is vulnerable to concurrent webhook deliveries unless there is a DB-level unique constraint or the operation is done atomically (e.g., upsert/transaction). The finding’s specific assertion that there is “no unique constraint on (userId, appId)” is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/migration shown), but the race-prone pattern itself is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A single boolean APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED couples both the inbound webhook and the outbound refresh/validation path, so configuring only the webhook secrets without CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT silently routes refreshes through the broken minimum-schema path and destroys stored credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the outbound refresh/validation path only uses the “minimum schema” when *both* `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`: `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) ... else schema.safeParse(...)`). Similarly, `refreshOAuthTokens` only routes to the external sync endpoint when the endpoint is configured. Therefore, configuring webhook secrets (and the encryption key) without `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` does **not** “silently route refreshes through the minimum-schema path,” and the described coupling-caused credential destruction is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook header name lookup doesn't lowercase the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME env value, so a case-mismatched name never matches Node's lowercased headers and every webhook permanently returns 403; also req.headers[...] can be a string[] for repeated headers, failing the string comparison silently

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. In Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase; if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set with any uppercase characters, this lookup will miss the header and always return 403 (the code does not lowercase/normalize the env value, only comments that it “should be in lowercase”). Additionally, `req.headers[...]` can be `string | string[] | undefined`; the strict comparison against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` will fail when it is a `string[]`, causing valid requests with repeated headers to be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts persists the Zod safeParse wrapper object instead of the parsed credential data, corrupting every Google credential on refresh so subsequent schema validation fails

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential `key` is now set to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. However `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not the parsed `data` itself. This would store the wrapper object in `credential.key`, corrupting the expected credential shape and likely causing later schema validation to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" as a placeholder when the provider's refresh response omits refresh_token, overwriting the user's real refresh token for O365 and permanently breaking authentication

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, it forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token data is merged into existing credentials via `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`, so this placeholder will overwrite the previously stored real `refresh_token`. The subsequent `prisma.credential.update` persists this bad value, causing future refreshes to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens sync-mode branch returns a raw fetch Response where callers expect provider-shaped objects, causing Google refresh to throw TypeError on res?.data, HubSpot to persist NaN expiry, and Zoho CRM/Bigin to throw on Response.data.error

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` in the sync-mode branch (`return response;` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`). Multiple callers still assume provider/axios/google-auth shaped return values: GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data; ... token.access_token` (will throw when `res` is a `Response` with no `.data`), and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM check `tokenInfo.data.error` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (will throw because `Response.data` is undefined). This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and breaks token refresh behavior when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The credential sync gate is global per-app-slug-per-user with no per-credential discriminator, so enabling sync reroutes all OAuth refreshes including credentials created through Cal.com's own OAuth flow, breaking those integrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the refresh path is gated only by global env/config, not by any per-credential/per-app opt-in. `refreshOAuthTokens` reroutes token refreshes whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), and many integrations now call it with `credential.userId`. There is no discriminator on whether the credential was created via Cal.com’s own OAuth flow vs via the new webhook. adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing the sync endpoint to receive a credential ID where it expects a user ID

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes a variable named `credentialId` as the third argument. But `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is `userId` (it sends it as `calcomUserId` in the POST body). Other integrations in the same diff consistently pass `credential.userId`. This suggests Zoho Bigin will send a credential ID where the sync endpoint expects a Cal.com user ID, breaking credential sync/refresh for that integration when enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Computed Zod keys like [z.string().toString()] produce the string key "[object Object]" instead of capturing expiry fields, and sync-mode parsing strips expiry_date/expires_in, breaking token-freshness tracking

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS this evaluates to a literal property name like `"[object Object]"`, not a pattern/catchall key, so the schema does not actually accept “any numeric expiry field” and will likely fail `safeParse` unless the response contains that exact key. Also, because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default and this schema is not `.passthrough()`, even if parsing succeeded it would drop fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`, which sync-mode relies on for token freshness. This is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret or signature), allowing anyone who can reach the endpoint to mint access tokens for arbitrary users

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, the code POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no secret header, signature, or token). This means the sync endpoint cannot verify the caller based on anything sent by Cal.com, so any party able to reach that endpoint could replicate the request and potentially obtain/mint tokens for arbitrary `calcomUserId` values, depending on the endpoint implementation. The diff introduces this unauthenticated outbound call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The app-credential webhook uses findFirst plus unconditional update, arbitrarily picking the first of multiple credentials and silently replacing a user's own OAuth credentials without consent or audit

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook updates credentials by doing `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and then `update` on that returned `id`. Because it uses `findFirst` with no ordering and no demonstrated uniqueness constraint in this diff, if multiple credential rows exist for the same `(userId, appId)` it could non-deterministically choose one to overwrite. The endpoint also unconditionally overwrites `credential.key` with decrypted `keys` (no audit/logging or additional checks beyond the shared secret), which is a concrete design/safety concern introduced by this change, though overwriting may be intended for “sync” behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws an unhandled ZodError resulting in a 500 instead of a 4xx, and there is no HTTP-method check so a GET with invalid body hits the same crash

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` with no try/catch or safeParse. A Zod validation failure will throw and (absent framework-level handling shown here) will result in a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. Additionally, there is no `req.method` guard (e.g., POST-only), so non-POST requests (like GET) can reach the same `parse(req.body)` path, increasing the likelihood of an exception when `req.body` is missing/invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh was rewritten as an eager, unconditional network call and DB write on every service construction instead of lazy refresh, causing latency and rate-limit exposure

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an unconditional refresh-token exchange (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) and then immediately updates the credential in DB via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. This refresh/update happens whenever this code path is executed (likely during service/connection setup), rather than being conditional on token expiry or performed lazily. That creates a concrete performance/rate-limit/extra-write concern grounded in the diff, but it’s not a verifiable correctness break on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce is the only OAuth app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens, so it is silently excluded from credential sync, creating inconsistent coverage

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lark sync-mode passes the raw sync endpoint response to handleLarkError which expects the Lark envelope {code, msg, data}, so Lark refresh fails in sync mode even when the sync endpoint succeeds

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound credential-sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no shared secret, HMAC, or signature, and doesn't enforce HTTPS, allowing unverified sync endpoints or DNS hijackers to inject attacker-chosen tokens into any user's credentials

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint app-credential.ts uses a single global shared secret with no per-app schema validation, no replay protection (nonce/timestamp), and non-constant-time secret comparison, enabling silent schema-unchecked overwrite of any user's credentials

adjudication_records.issue_text: `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", making the schema require a key named "[object Object]" so every real token response fails safeParse and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" for valid responses whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set (breaking credential-sync for Google, Zoom, O365, and unconditionally breaking Salesforce token refresh)

adjudication_records.issue_text: `zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-86`: `refreshOAuthTokens` is passed `credentialId` as the `userId` argument instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint receives the credential's row ID as `calcomUserId` and syncs tokens against the wrong user identity

adjudication_records.issue_text: `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `response.statusText !== "OK"` is an unreliable success check since statusText is locale/implementation-dependent; `response.ok` should be used instead

Using `response.ok` or checking `response.status` would be the correct, robust success check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:257-265`: O365 parse-failure behavior silently changed from log-and-continue to throw, so a transient malformed Microsoft token response (previously tolerated) now fails event creation for O365 users through the booking flow

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10 uses [z.string().toString()] as computed schema keys, which evaluate to "[object Object]" rather than allowing other properties, so zod strips all fields except access_token — losing expiry_date (Google) and instance_url/signature/issued_at/id (Salesforce) that readers expect

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-94 unconditionally refreshes via login.salesforce.com and wholesale-replaces the stored credential key on every service instantiation, deleting any fields the refresh response omits with no read-modify-write merge or app-level validation
